title: Replace virtual includes generated paths with their actual paths in the coverage reports.

timeline.body:
Fixes #6254.

RELNOTES: The code coverage report now includes the actual paths to header files instead of the ugly, 
Bazel generated, virtual includes path. 

For example, the `SF:` (source file) lines in the coverage report now look like this:
```
SF:include/common/strategy.h
```
instead of
```
SF:bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/bin/include/common/_virtual_includes/strategy/strategy.h
```

SuperNit: Thank you for adding comments! Pls add spaces around rootFiles, also everywhere below (pardon internal only link: https://engdoc.corp.google.com/eng/doc/devguide/java/practices/methods.md?cl=head#call-site-literals)

timeline.body: I'd not be afraid to add param comments here :P

reply.body: I didn't add any here because this takes empty everything to create an empty object, so IMO it's not so relevant to know what each param does.

timeline.body: Parsing will fail when files contain : in their name, won't it? Let's store paths in some escaped format?

reply.body: I was wondering when that could happen... do you have any ideas? And any ideas how to escape this? Any other character would have the same problem, wouldn't it?

timeline.body: Will this cause problems on Windows/Mac where newline separator is different?

reply.body: Thanks, I didn't realize this can be different on other OSs. Changed with System.lineSeparator() .

timeline.body: Let's make this at least LinkedHashMap, or maybe even better ImmutableMap.Builder? To keep the order of files deterministic?

reply.body: Hmm now I'm thinking, if we should make it a NestedSet of Pairs instead, to not be quadratic in used memory, and then create the Map only when actually iterating the map. Wdyt?
Some good ideas here, thanks. I ended up with a nested set of pairs and a lazy write action, that will unflatten the nested set at execution time.

timeline.body: This is roughly an equivalent of iterating a nested set in analysis, isn't it? Is there an easy way to move this to execution?

reply.body: Yup, see my other comment: I ended up with a nested set of pairs and a lazy write action, that will unflatten the nested set at execution time.

timeline.body:
Up to you, my thinking with param comments is to add them whenever it's not clear what the comment represents from the variable name. I also put them in the constructors for EMPTY objects, as it simplifies understanding of "what goes into the constructor".

I agree that we do this only because the IDE is not helping with this already, but I still like them :)
